En cas de groupement conjoint, le mandataire sera solidaire, pour l'exécution du marché public, de chacun des membres du groupement, pour ses obligations contractuelles à l'égard de l’acheteur. references_experience.text: énements : 2 formats de kakémonos (80x200 cm) pour les événements du projet (conférences, salons, ateliers). quelques éléments graphiques génériques permettant de décliner l’identité sur les supports de communication du projet. Supports pédagogiques illustrés destinés aux enseignants : conception d'une série de supports visuels (affiches, posters pédagogiques) présentant de manière ludique et accessible le projet EARTH-LIFE (primaire, collège, lycée). insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

staffing_team.text: s; 2. Demonstrates a credible, technically viable, and sound approach across all four technical focus areas, backed by veriﬁable commercial experience; 3. Presents a robust, low-risk operational strategy that guarantees 24x7 legacy sustainment and zero disruption during modernization; 4. Clearly documents commercial solution maturity and satisﬁes statutory criteria for the applicable award instrument (FAR Part 12 or 10 U.S.C. § 4022); 5. Provides a measurable, outcome-oriented PWS framework aligned to Draft SOO objectives; 6. Demonstrates actionable alignment with Zero Trust, DHA cloud security, and RMF; and 7. Details a realistic staffing pipeline meeting security clearance and facility access criteria. The Government reserves the right to invite to Phase II only those Go-rated offerors whose submissions demonstrate the highest technical merit and lowest operational transition risk. A submission that does not meet all Go criteria will receive a No-Go rating and will not advance. 3.3 Phase II Preview — Oral Presentation, Demonstration, and Targeted Validation The Government may invite selected vendors receiving a Phase I Go rating to participate in Phase II oral presentations, live demonstrations, technical challenges, written question- and-answer exchanges, or a comb

ombination of these methods. Phase II instructions and evaluation criteria will be provided only to selected vendors. To validate solution maturity, feasibility, and alignment with Government objectives, the Government may request one or more of the following: 1. Oral presentation or live demonstration of relevant commercial capabilities; 2. Clariﬁcation or reﬁnement of the Technical Solution Brief, Draft SOO Crosswalk, or draft performance-based work statement; 3. A proposed performance-measurement and surveillance approach addressing key operational, cybersecurity, modernization, and delivery outcomes; 4. A high-level resource and staffing approach; 5. A preliminary ROM or other commercial-pricing information; and 6.
